edges.notes: Linux capabilities (CAP_* sets on thread credentials) are defined by the kernel security/credentials model per documented manuals.
User namespaces interact with capability maps; capabilities are privilege decomposition, not namespace view isolation.
Container stacks compose capability dropping with cgroup resource limits; distinct mechanisms.
LSM (SELinux/AppArmor-class) layers MAC policy on top of capability checks; not the same abstraction.
seccomp filters syscalls; capabilities gate whether privileged operations are permitted when invoked.
Docker exposes capability add/drop for Linux containers per common deployment understanding.
Kubernetes securityContext can adjust Linux capabilities for pods/containers.
containerd passes OCI/Linux capability options when creating containers.
runc applies capability-related options from OCI Linux config when starting bundles.
Podman configures Linux capabilities for rootless and rootful containers.
CRI-O applies capability settings for Kubernetes workloads on Linux.
systemd unit and ambient capability settings interact with service credentials on Linux.
Installing netfilter firewall rules typically requires network administration capabilities (e.g. CAP_NET_ADMIN) on Linux.
